questions_for_integrator: Does wheel_track 0.16 m reduce line_loss_events below 1.0 per run on the s-bend and slalom, given that radius 0.035 m did not?
If line loss persists, at what progress does the first loss occur on each track? Does it sit at the same point on every track, which would suggest the start or a fixed bend?
Does steering_oscillation rise with the wider track (above about 0.2 would suggest overshoot)?
Do the wheels slip on starts at 0.16 m track, and does completion_time approach 3 s on any track?

intent: Test one turn-authority change against iteration 4: widen wheel_track from 0.14 m to 0.16 m, keeping the seven 16 mm sensors at y = 0.03 m across ±3 cm, wheel_radius 0.035 m and mass 0.6 kg. A wider track gives more yaw rate for the same wheel-speed difference. Expected result: line_loss_events at or below 0.5 per run on the s-bend and slalom, max_error under 0.06 m, and progress above the iteration 4 values.
learning: Sensing (span, offset) and mass each left line loss at 1.0 per run, and so did wheel radius. If wider track also fails, the loss is probably not a turn-authority limit. The next test should then return to the iteration 0 sensing (5 sensors, 12 mm, y 0.05 m), which gave the best score so far (52.28), and check whether the progress gap comes from the sensing rather than the dynamics.
rationale: Iterations 0 to 4 have now varied sensor span (4 cm and 6 cm), forward offset (y 0.05, 0.04, 0.03), mass (0.8, 0.7, 0.6 kg) and wheel radius (0.03, 0.035 m). Line_loss_events stayed at about 1.0 per run in every case, and steering oscillation stayed between 0.07 and 0.14, so the robot is not jittering. Iteration 4 is the decisive result. The integration rule for the case where line loss persists after the radius change says that wheel radius is not the limit and that turn authority is the next lever. Iteration 4 scored 46.77, above iteration 3 (46.16) but below the best iteration 0 (52.28). The score is driven mainly by progress, which the sensing changes in iterations 1 to 3 reduced. I therefore keep the iteration 4 base (y 0.03, ±3 cm span, 16 mm sensors, mass 0.6 kg, radius 0.035 m) and change one thing: wheel_track from 0.14 to 0.16 m. Track width sets the yaw rate per unit wheel-speed difference, so this is the untested turn-authority step that the Integrator's rules name. Expected result: line_loss_events at or below 0.5 per run on the s-bend and slalom, max_error under 0.06 m, and progress above the iteration 4 values (oval 0.11, s-bend 0.1325, slalom 0.0971). If line loss still stays at 1.0, the cause is probably a fixed point on the course, such as the start or one bend, rather than geometry. The next step would then be to return toward the iteration 0 sensing (5 sensors, 12 mm, y 0.05), which gave the highest progress so far, and to request telemetry on where the loss occurs.
